transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I’m having trouble going near the front windows at work, or even that part of the street. I keep making excuses to stay in the back, even though being up front is part of my job. It’s getting hard to deal with.
Do you feel intense fear or panic when you are near the front windows or that part of the street?

Yes. When I get near those front windows or that part of the street, I kind of freeze up and just can’t make myself go there. I’ve been making excuses to stay in the back, even though I know it’s part of my job to be up front.

Can you tell me more about why you avoid the front windows and that part of the street? Is it because you're worried about being in open spaces, or is it more about being seen or judged by others in that area?

It’s not really about open spaces, or people judging me. It’s that I just can’t make myself go near those front windows or that part of the street anymore. I keep coming up with reasons to stay in the back, even though I know being up front is part of my job.
Has this avoidance been happening for a long time, or did it start suddenly? And do you feel fear even when you’re just thinking about going near those front windows or that part of the street?

It started pretty suddenly. It’s been about two weeks now, ever since a car crashed through the store window during my overnight shift. And yeah, even just thinking about going near those front windows or that part of the street makes me feel scared.

latest_inference.note: This turn added F43.10 (Post-traumatic stress disorder) as the presenting symptoms of sudden onset avoidance, fear in proximity to a specific location, and intrusive thoughts following a traumatic event (car crash through store window) align with PTSD. Other anxiety disorders (F40.00, F40.10, F40.20) were ruled out as the avoidance is trauma-related rather than due to agoraphobia, social anxiety, or specific phobia.
